name: Xero
tagline: Cloud accounting, invoicing, bank reconciliation, payroll add-ons, and reporting

pricing.notes: Official US pricing checked 2026-07-30; Early listed at $25/month after promotional discounts, with higher Growing/Established tiers.

verdictSummary: Invoices and reports are buildable, but Xero's real product is bank feeds, accounting workflows, accountant collaboration, compliance expectations, integrations, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Build simple bookkeeping with invoices, expenses, CSV imports, chart of accounts, and reports for personal/internal use.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because businesses need dependable books, not just a ledger UI.

priorArt.name: Odoo
priorArt.desc: Open-source business suite with accounting modules; heavier than a solo DIY clone.

alternatives.name: ERPNext
alternatives.desc: Accounting, invoices, reconciliation, inventory and payroll in one free ERP; the server becomes another account to reconcile.

alternatives.name: Manager Desktop
alternatives.desc: A full local ledger with invoices and reconciliation; there is no shared cloud unless you provide one.

alternatives.name: Bigcapital
alternatives.desc: Modern double-entry books, expenses and inventory in Docker; live bank feeds are not magically free.

alternatives.name: LedgerSMB
alternatives.desc: Serious accounting, invoicing, stock and reports; the interface is less polished and more interested in balancing.

alternatives.name: Frappe Books
alternatives.desc: Offline invoices, bills, payments and reports with a real ledger; multi-user cloud work is absent.

alternatives.name: Odoo Accounting — One App Free
alternatives.desc: A hosted accounting app for zero dollars; add another unrelated Odoo app and the meter starts.

alternatives.name: Dolibarr
alternatives.desc: Invoices, banks, stock and double-entry accounting in one practical suite; native payroll is not included.

alternatives.name: GnuCash
alternatives.desc: Desktop double-entry books, invoicing and reports; bank automation and collaboration are the losses.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Akaunting
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free base is single-entry unless you buy the Double-Entry app, and the repo is BSL rather than open source.

notes: Another structural no due regulatory/financial integrations.
prompt:
Build me a freelancer bookkeeping app covering the personal slice of Xero:
invoices, expenses, and quarterly reports. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3; income and expense entries
  with date, amount, category, client, and an attached receipt file.
- CSV import from my bank's export, plus a rules table (description pattern to
  category) so repeat transactions auto-categorize.
- Invoices numbered sequentially, rendered to PDF with pdfkit, one paid/unpaid
  flag. Nothing more.
- Reports: quarterly income, expenses by category, and a one-page cash P&L I
  can print for my accountant.
- Binds to localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry; write a nightly copy of
  the SQLite file to a dated backup.
- Out of scope: bank feeds, reconciliation, payroll, tax filing, and audit
  history. Do not build any of them; if I need real accounting, Odoo or
  Invoice Ninja is the honest route.
- README: state that this is a ledger for staying organized between real tools,
  not accounting. Xero's product is bank feeds, reconciliation, and books an
  accountant will accept, and no one should sign off these numbers unchecked.
